prior_narrative.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose weekly grouping of unrelated RL items, not a developing story. Recent entries range from a fuzz-testing method for safety-critical RL agents to Moonshot AI's open-sourced AgentENV framework for scaling agentic RL training.
prior_narrative.whats_new: A new arXiv paper, ResidencyRL, applies reinforcement learning to simulate clinical-residency training — modeling how physicians build expertise through staged patient encounters and feedback.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Unlike the two research papers here, AgentENV is a released open-source framework, not a benchmark result — the one item in this batch platform engineers can actually adopt rather than just read.

beats.headline: Fuzz-testing paper probes safety-critical RL agents for unexpected failure modes
beats.summary: New arXiv work evaluates fuzz testing as a method to surface unexpected RL-agent behaviors before deployment in robotics, autonomous driving, and drone control.

beats.headline: Moonshot AI and kvcache-ai open-source AgentENV to scale agentic RL
beats.summary: New open-source framework targets scaling agentic reinforcement learning training — a shipped tool, not an academic result like the papers alongside it.

beats.headline: ResidencyRL simulates clinical-residency training as an RL problem
beats.summary: New arXiv work models how physicians convert academic knowledge into clinical judgment through simulated patient encounters with staged feedback, mirroring real residency training.

open_questions: Does the fuzz-testing methodology surface failures that existing RL safety evals miss, or mostly duplicate them?
Does AgentENV's scaling approach hold up against existing agentic-RL training frameworks, or is it mainly a Moonshot-internal tool going public?
Does ResidencyRL's simulated training transfer to real clinical decision-making, or only to the benchmark's synthetic cases?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Scaling agentic RL training? Check AgentENV's repo before building a custom scaling harness — it's the one item in this batch that's a shipped tool, not the two narrower academic results (safety-critical RL fuzz testing, simulated clinical-residency training) alongside it.
